correctness.rationale: The implication stays in a box and cannot cross boxes at distance at least three. A new symbol in just one coordinate can be propagated over the base box one distance-one step at a time: the new-symbol word at the old base and the old-symbol word at the next base are the two distance-two premises. For a point at distance two, the first rectangle supplies the two one-symbol extensions, after which both can be absorbed. Traversing a distance-one spanning tree in the second box extends this to the box merge. The resulting greedy process stays in the actual closure and terminates in a closed cover of the seed, so it yields the closure for any merge order. For a closed set the distance-one components are precisely the boxes; the merge lemma rules out components at distance two. This includes the empty union. Coordinate coverage forces k≥1+M, and for a merge the rank Σ(|Bᵢ|−1) increases over the sum of the two ranks by Σ(1−|Bᵢ∩Dᵢ|)≤2, proving the other lower bound. For attainment, if the largest symbol class dominates, pair each other token with a distinct token of that class. Otherwise pair from two largest classes: with n tokens and each class at most ceil(n/2), any class attaining that cap must be among the two selected, so after removal the new cap ceil((n−2)/2) is maintained. The construction yields max(M,ceil(T/2)) groups. With the common base word, the group words generate all one-change words and then all words by the rectangle rule and induction on support. In dimension one this gives exactly q₁, consistent with there being no triggers.
residual_risks: Finite fixture checks are only corroborative. The exact-distance-two condition is necessary; the argument does not certify other convexities or arbitrary Horn systems.

evidence: For ordinary P₃ the published product proof already transports a corner across two different factors. Its Corollary 2 and Lemmas 3–5 use full-or-singleton coordinates and control the growth of dimension under near merges. Dourado et al.'s available abstract concerns complexity on chordal graphs and an interval-graph algorithm; the exact same induced rule is the relevant one, but full text was not accessible. Bichoupan's abstract treats general implication-basis complexity.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The proof mechanism for product structure and merging is not wholly new: the corner-transport part of the ordinary proof also works for induced paths. But ordinary convexity forces full clique fibres and bounds dimension rather than counting individual symbol capacities. It does not give the unrestricted box structure or the sharp symbol-sensitive rank and matching formula.

evidence: Their rank surrogate is the number of active factors, with gain at most two. In the frozen result the sum of excess symbol counts is the right quantity and a single-factor supply constraint also binds. The proof of attainment pairs tokens from different coordinates.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The heterogeneous statement adapts known merging geometry, but deriving its precise law requires a different rank estimate and a matching construction; it is not a corollary of the numeric ordinary or geodesic results. In the binary specialization these distinctions disappear and the value and structural recursion were already covered.

evidence: Induced-P₃ endpoints in a clique product are exactly at Hamming distance two, with the two missing rectangle corners as common neighbors. The shortest-path interval allows all coordinatewise choices for endpoint pairs of any distance; {000,111} stays closed for induced P₃ but geodesically generates all of Q₃.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The statement is exactly induced-P₃ closure, coincides with geodesic closure only when dimension is at most two on this domain, and coincides with ordinary P₃ on binary products. Equality of geodesic and induced generator counts when T≤2M does not identify those two closures.

originality.rationale: The structural recursion has a strong antecedent in ordinary P₃ convexity: connected hulls factor and nearby subproducts can merge, and in the binary case the two rules coincide. The supported distinct result is the exact induced-P₃ structure with arbitrary coordinate symbol subsets and its sharp heterogeneous generator count. Ordinary P₃ hulls fill an entire clique fibre as soon as there are two symbols in it; that operation is unavailable for induced P₃. The known geodesic result has a different closure and generator count in general.
residual_risks: Exact overlap in uninspected induced-path literature or differently named closure theory is not ruled out. No full-document noncoverage inference is made for the unavailable papers. The binary recursion and hull number are not original claims.

value.rationale: Separated product components are a canonical description of the actual implication closure, making the box-merge algorithm exact rather than just an upper bound. The minimum generator formula distinguishes a single large alphabet's supply constraint from the total two-symbol growth budget. Those are natural structural features not detected by the established dimension-only ordinary-P₃ result.
residual_risks: The description does not bound complexity in a compressed input representation or determine a minimum implication basis.
